title: Fishbone stitch
subtitle: Overlapping slanted stitches that meet at a central spine to fill leaf shapes
excerpt: Fishbone stitch fills a leaf or petal shape with pairs of slanted stitches that meet along a central spine. The stitches overlap slightly at the centre line, creating a solid fill with a neat ridge down the middle.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), fishbone stitch entry.

content.text: Fishbone stitch fills a pointed shape by working pairs of diagonal stitches from the outer edge toward a centre spine. Each pair meets at the spine, with one stitch from the left side and one from the right. The stitches overlap at the centre by about 2 mm, which locks them down and creates the characteristic ridge. Working from the tip of the leaf toward the base keeps the shape tidy.
Transfer the leaf outline and draw a light pencil line down the centre from tip to base. Secure the thread on the back.

Bring the needle up at A, the very tip of the leaf, on the centre line. Make one short straight stitch down the spine to B, about 3 mm. This is the starting stitch that the first pair of diagonals will overlap.
Bring the needle up at C on the left edge of the leaf, level with B. Insert at D, crossing the spine by about 2 mm to the right of B. This is the first left-side stitch.
Bring the needle up at E on the right edge of the leaf, level with C. Insert at F, crossing the spine by about 2 mm to the left of the previous stitch's entry. This is the matching right-side stitch.
Continue working pairs from left then right, stepping down the leaf toward the base. Keep each stitch angled toward the tip so the spine ridge stays clear. Fill to the base and secure the thread.

items.symptom: The spine ridge is not visible
items.cause: Stitches are meeting exactly at the centre line rather than crossing it by 2 mm.
items.fix: Each stitch should travel 2 mm past the centre line. A slight overlap at the spine is correct, not a mistake.

items.symptom: The fill is uneven near the base of the leaf
items.cause: Stitches were kept at a fixed angle even as the shape widened, leaving bare patches.
items.fix: Increase the angle of the diagonals as the leaf widens so each pair reaches the outer edge of the shape.
